adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51 — The 10s legacy-write timeout context is derived from the incoming request ctx (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`), so when the parent request context is canceled at the end of the HTTP request (as k8s apiserver request contexts are), the derived child context is canceled too, aborting the async legacy write early regardless of the 10s budget.

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, the async legacy writes are started in goroutines after the storage operation returns (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). Each goroutine derives its timeout context from the incoming `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` (e.g., `Create`: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)`). Because child contexts are canceled when the parent `ctx` is canceled, any cancellation of the request context will immediately cancel the legacy-write context, potentially aborting the intended async legacy write before the 10s budget elapses. This can cause legacy writes to be skipped/partial, breaking the intended dual-write behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Update's async legacy write error is only recorded as a metric with no logging, and unlike the pre-change code no longer re-fetches/re-derives the object for Legacy.Update, so on races/retries the legacy store can silently drift from Storage with no error trail.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the legacy write is moved into a goroutine and its error is never logged—only `recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...)` is called (no `log.Error` inside the async block). Also, the previous implementation ensured Legacy received the same computed updated object (via `UpdatedObject` + `updateWrapper`), whereas the new code passes the original `objInfo` to both `Storage.Update` and (later) `Legacy.Update`; this can cause `UpdatedObjectInfo` to be evaluated twice and potentially yield different objects, allowing legacy to diverge silently from storage.
